items.title: Interneurons and network activity in the cerebral cortex: a developmental dialogue
items.author: Oscar Marín
items.content: Neuronal activity is traditionally viewed as instructing cortical interneuron development. In this Review, Moissidis and Marín discuss how interneurons also actively shape early postnatal network activity, establishing a reciprocal dialogue that drives the maturation of both interneurons and cortical circuits.

items.title: The endocannabinoid system and the ageing brain
items.author: Andreas Zimmer
items.content: Age-related changes in endocannabinoid system (ECS) activity might contribute to the decline in cognitive function observed during ageing. In this review, Andreas Zimmer discusses how evidence from genetic and pharmacological studies in mice and humans indicate that relevant cognitive functions may change as a result of changing ECS activity.

items.title: A defined brainstem circuit for cardiac control
items.author: Sian Lewis
items.content: A distinct neuropeptide Y2 receptor-expressing neuronal subtype is identified in the brainstem nucleus ambiguus that selectively projects to cardiac ganglia and regulates heart rate and the mammalian diving reflex.

items.title: Brain regulation of bile acids
items.author: Darran Yates
items.content: A new study in mice reveals that bile acid homeostasis in the liver is regulated by neurons from the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus.

items.title: Sensing the skeleton: sensorineural regulation in bone
items.author: Aaron W. James
items.content: The skeleton is innervated by neurons that convey sensory information to the CNS and release neuroregulatory peptides to influence the bone microenvironment. James and colleagues describe the mechanisms underlying sensorineural regulation of skeletal bone, the contributions of nerve–bone coupling to bone growth and repair, and the disruption of this axis in various skeletal pathologies.

items.title: In situ capture of combinatorial neuromodulatory codes
items.author: Peter N. Kalugin
items.content: In this Tools of the Trade article, Peter Kalugin discusses the development of multiplexed optical recording of sensors on a micro-endoscope (MORSE) to track combinatorial hormone, neurotransmitter, and neuromodulator signals on the spatial and temporal scale of neural activity.

items.title: Creating space for human organoids in the mouse brain
items.author: Katherine Whalley
items.content: Transplantation of human cortical organoids into ‘apallial’ mice facilitates their integration and provides opportunities to study human cortical development and disease.
